extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (advanced undergraduates may also use this as a reference)
extracted.subtask_description: Index/reference excerpt from a graduate-level algebraic geometry textbook listing named theorems, criteria, and properties (e.g., flatness, Jacobian criterion, ampleness criteria) with brief notes on their uses and behavior. Useful as a compact map of which theorems/criteria check which geometric/algebraic properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Flatness (various remarks and tests): preserved by base change; open condition; open in good situations; behavior over a field; criterion over Discrete Valuation Rings; behavior over dual numbers, integral domains, principal ideal domains; sends associated points to associated points; slicing criterion for flatness; stalk-local / stalk/prime-local property; topological aspects; transitivity; valuative criterion; variation of cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes list many ways flatness is tested and behaves: open/valuative/slicing criteria; preserved under base-change; stalk-local nature; special cases over DVRs, dual numbers, PIDs; related to variation of cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: generic flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic flatness — referenced (121, 682–684) with an 'improved version' (683).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assert that a morphism is flat over a dense open of the base (Generic Freeness/Grothendieck Generic Freeness Lemma cited nearby).

rubrics_metrics.name: generic smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic smoothness — listed for varieties; occurrences 'on source' and 'on target' (701–703).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard criterion that a morphism is smooth over a dense open of the base; the index indicates separate considerations for source vs target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic Freeness Lemma / Grothendieck’s Generic Freeness Lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic Freeness Lemma — referenced (682, 682, 683) / Grothendieck’s Generic Freeness Lemma (see Generic Freeness Lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool to get a dense open over which a finitely generated module becomes free; tied to generic flatness and families behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Jacobian criterion — appears with occurrences: (362, 364–366, 368, 370, 383, 533, 582, 583, 594, 595). Notes: 'for projective hypersurfaces', 'for smoothness', 'description of Ω, map, matrix', 'Jacobian corank function', 'Jacobian test for projective hypersurfaces'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index records that the Jacobian (matrix/corank) is used to test smoothness and to study projective hypersurfaces; also references to description of the module of differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleiman’s numerical criterion for ampleness
rubrics_metrics.description: Kleiman’s numerical criterion for ampleness — listed; see also Nakai-Moishezon criterion for ampleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A numerical criterion to decide ampleness using intersection numbers and the nef cone; index cross-references related ampleness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakai–Moishezon criterion for ampleness
rubrics_metrics.description: Nakai–Moishezon criterion for ampleness — listed and cross-referenced with Kleiman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion characterizing ampleness via positivity of intersection numbers on all subvarieties; index groups it with other ampleness tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kodaira’s criterion for ampleness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic/algebro-geometric ampleness criterion (Kodaira embedding type results); listed among ampleness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre’s criterion for normality
rubrics_metrics.description: Serre’s criterion for normality — referenced in relation to normality (see also Serre’s criterion for normality, 733, 740, 742, 756, 757, 760).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard algebraic test (R1 + S2) for a scheme/ring to be normal; index points to multiple places discussing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull’s Principal Ideal Theorem (and Krull’s Height/Intersection theorems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Krull’s Principal Ideal Theorem — listed (271, 333, 346, 347, 371, 372, 383) with mentions 'for tangent spaces'. Krull’s Height Theorem and Krull Intersection Theorem also appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorems controlling heights of prime ideals and intersections; used as structural criteria (e.g., dimension bounds, tangent space bounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracle Flatness Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Miracle Flatness Theorem — cited (733, 738, 739, 780) with note 'algebraic version, locally ringed spaces' and related references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion giving flatness from Cohen–Macaulayness plus fiber-dimension conditions; index indicates algebraic and locally ringed space versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck’s Coherence Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Grothendieck’s Coherence Theorem — referenced many times (323, 410, 449, 477, 483, 484, 512, 518–520, 572, 713, 752, 756, 765–767) and 'for projective morphisms' (485).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coherence results for higher direct images and pushforwards under proper/projective morphisms; used to check coherence of sheaves arising from geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama’s Lemma (and geometric version)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental local algebra criterion about generating sets modulo maximal ideals; geometric Nakayama used to deduce generation statements on fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-Down and Going-Up Theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Going-Down Theorem — referenced 'for finite extensions of integrally closed domains' and other contexts (713, 714, 717). Going-Up Theorem — (232, 331, 339, 680).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorems controlling prime lying-over/chain behavior under integral extensions; used to analyze integrality and specialization of primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullstellensatz (including from dimension theory)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic geometry basic criterion linking vanishing ideals and variety points; index indicates multiple proofs/uses (including dimension-theoretic derivations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Noether normalization — referenced (305, 334, 335, 337, 338, 353, 354) and 'geometric Noether normalization'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure/theorem to reduce rings/schemes to finite maps from affine space; used as a tool/criterion for finiteness and dimension arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalization (integral closure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalization / integral closure — 'is integral and surjective', 'is birational morphism', 'not flat', 'finiteness of integral closure' (301–305, 331, 380, 386, 459, 460, 467, 468, 470, 471, 516, 533, 539, 602, 606, 675, 677, 751, 757, 762, 774).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index describes properties/tests about normalization: finiteness, behavior under field extensions, when it fails to be flat, and its birational/integral/surjective nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersection number invariance in flat families
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection number / product of L1,...,Ln with F — 'locally constant in flat families' (690), 'deformation invariance' (561), 'is symmetric multilinear' (562); on a surface (566).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records that intersection numbers are deformation/flat-family invariants and lists algebraic properties used to check numerical invariants (symmetry, multilinearity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grauert’s Theorem (coherence/semicontinuity statements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic/coherent direct image results and semicontinuity type statements used to test constancy/coherence of higher direct images in families.
